The Police Inspector of Jnanabharathi Police Station, Bangalore, has submitted charge sheet against
the accused for the offences punishable U/s.306 of Indian Penal Code in their Crime No.311/2016.
2.

The factual matrix of the prosecution case are as under:
The marriage of accused was solemnized with the deceased-Smt.Bhuvaneshwari on 23.06.2003 at Bangalore, and out of the wedlock they blessed with two female children.
After the marriage the accused subjected deceased-Smt. Bhuvaneshwari to physical and mental cruelty, as she has failed to be get male child.

Since one year the accused and deceased started to reside in a house bearing No.6, First Floor, 10 th Cross, Vidhana Soudha layout Papareddypalya within the limits of Jnanabharathi P.S., Bangalore, at that time the accused by receiving entire salary of the deceased,
harassing her by abusing and assaulting in demanding to bring money, on demand of accused, complainant has got transferred the amount to the account of accused and deceased-Smt. Bhuvaneshwari.
Even though after receipt of the money, the accused harassing the deceased physically and mentally.
Unable to bear the same, and by feeling hurt the deceased committed suicide by hanging at her matrimonial house.
The accused by subjecting the deceased - Smt.Bhuvaneshwari to physical and mental cruelty abetted her to commit suicide and thereby the accused has committed the offence as alleged against him.

3.The Jnanabharathi Police have submitted charge sheet before the jurisdictional IX Addl., CMM.,
Bangalore.
The learned Magistrate took cognizance of the offence and committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. after furnishing charge sheet copy to the accused [erspms.

The same was numbered as SC No.316/2017.
4.The charge was framed against the accused on 30.07.2018 for the offences punishable U/s.498A and 306 of IPC.
The accused has pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
5.The prosecution has examined nine witnesses as PW.1 to PW.8 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to P8 and identified MO1 to 5.
On consent of learned counsel for accused Inquest and PM Report were marked at Ex.P4 and P5.
As such the learned Public Prosecutor given up the witnesses CW.10.
In view of the available evidence of other police official witnesses, the learned Public Prosecutor has given up the witnesses CW.4 to CW.6, CW.11 and CW.12.
The witness cited as CW.15 has not been examined by the prosecution due to failure of concerned police to secure the said witness and keep present before the Court for the purpose of evidence.

So the evidence of prosecution was taken as closed with an opportunity to examine the said witness CW.15, if the said witness was secured and produced by the concerned police before the Court for examination before conclusion of the trial.
6.After completion of prosecution side evidence, this Court has recorded the statement of accused on 7.1.2023 as provided U/s.313 of Cr.P.C.

1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused being husband, while residing in a house No.6, First Floor, 10th Cross, Vidhana Soudha layout Papareddypalya within the limits of Jnanabharathi P.S., Bangalore,
subjected deceased- Smt.Bhuvaneshwari to physical and mental cruelty by abusing and assaulting and thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable under Section 498-A of IPC?

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused being the husband while residing in a house No.6, First Floor, 10th Cross, Vidhana Soudha layout Papareddypalya within the limits of Jnanabharathi P.S., Bangalore, subjected deceased- Smt.Bhuvaneshawri, to physical and mental cruelty by abusing and assaulting and o, unable to bear the same, and by feeling hurt the deceased on 27.11.2016 in between 12.30 p.m. and 12.50 p.m.

After marriage the deceased-Smt.
Bhuvaneshwari and accused were residing at Vijayanagar, Bangalore.
There was minor difference between them, however, they were leading happy married life in spite of minor differences.
The accused has not harassed the deceased.
After 14 years of marriage his daughter committed suicide in the matrimonial house situated at Vidhana Soudha Layout.
Reasons for suicide of his daughter is not known.
He did not file any complaint against accused regarding dowry harassment to his daughter.
His signature was obtained on Ex.P1 complainant when he was under pressure.
He does not know the contents of the complaint.
Ex.P2 Mahazar was not drawn in his presence.
He has not remember as to whether his further statement was recorded by the I.O., PW.1 has been treated as hostile witness and cross-examined by the learned Public Prosecutor.
Nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to establish the contents of Ex.P1 complaint and Ex.P2 Mahazar.
Further statement given by the PW.1marked as Ex.P3 is also denied.
Alleged physical and mental harassment meted by the deceased has not been spoken by PW.1.
12.PW.2 Harish being the brother of the deceased-Smt. Bhuvaneshwari, deposed that about 20 years back his sister marriage was solemnized with the accused at Bangalore.
It was love marriage.
His family members did not agree for the said marriage.
However, marriage was performed as per the wishes of his sister.
After marriage deceased-Smt. Bhuvaneshwari and accused were residing at Vijayanagar, Bangalore, and thereafter they shifted to Vidhana Soudha Layout.
His sister was working at Bangalore.
The accused and his sister blessed with two female children.
After giving birth to female children, his sister meted out harassment by the accused.
The accused assaulted on the deceased on several occasions, and the deceased took treatment.
The deceased gave complaint before the police in this regard.
His father and mother advised his sister to take divorce if she is not willing to lead life with the accused, as his sister was an Engineering Graduate.
When a complaint was lodged before Vijayanagar Police, he requested his friend PW.3 Devaraj to visit the house of the accused, and to speak to his sister regarding her future course of action.
Accordingly, PW.3 Devaraj and CW.5 Nagaraj visited the house of the accused.

PW.3 Devaraj and CW.5 Nagaraj spoke to accused to express his opinion as to whether he is willing to continue relationship with the deceased- Smt. Bhuvaneshwari, otherwise deceased will take her own decision to lead her life.

After visit of PW.3 and CW.5 to the house of the accused, he was at Holenarasipura for a period of one week, at that time his sister telephoned to his father, and requested his father to make an alternative arrangement for her.
Meanwhile the accused telephoned to his father and threatened that he will finish the deceased.
His father told the accused, that he will make an alternative arrangement for his daughter, till then not to harass the deceased.
His sister committed suicide on 27.11.2016, in the matrimonial house situated at Vidhana Soudha Layout.

The accused telephoned him and informed (By The Learned Public Prosecutor) vs Complainant Has Got Transferred The ... on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93270603/
4 him regarding the death of his sister.
He told the accused not to remove the body till his visit to Bangalore.
He rushed to Bangalore, and saw the dead body of his sister and a complaint was filed before Jnanabharathi P.S.,
The accused is responsible for the suicidal death of his sister.

During the cross-examination by the learned counsel for the accused, PW.2 deposed that his family members did not agree for the marriage between deceased-Smt.Bhuvaneshwari and accused, accused and deceased were working in MNC Company at Bangalore, both of them were getting handsome salary,
he never telephoned to his sister after marriage, but his sister used to call him through phone.
He never visited the house of the accused and deceased- Smt. Bhuvaneshwari, but he denies that he is not aware about the matrimonial relationship between accused and deceased- Smt. Bhuvaneshwari.
Physical and mental harassment meted out by the deceased, soon before her death has been denied by the learned counsel for the accused.
PW.2 did not file any complaint regarding the strained matrimonial relationship between the accused and the deceased, when they were leading married life at Bangalore.
He gave statement before the Police that the accused tortured his sister for not giving birth to male child.
He denies that his sister was neglected due to her love marriage with the accused, and his sister mentally suffered a lot due to behaviour of her blood relatives.
Telephone call by the deceased to her father as deposed by PW.2 has not been corroborated by PW.1 S. Erappa being the father of the deceased.
Therefore, based on the evidence of PW.2 alone it cannot be said that the accused abetted the deceased-Smt. Bhuvaneshwari to commit suicide.

13.In (2019) 17 Supreme Court Cases 301 (Ude Singh And others Versus State of Haryana) Hon'ble Supreme Court held that "Aabetment" involves a mental process of instigating a person in doing something.

entities.text: (2019) 17 Supreme Court Cases 301 (Ude Singh And others Versus State of Haryana)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
A person abets the doing of a thing when:
(i) he instigates any person to do that thing; or (ii) he engages with one or more persons in any conspiracy for the doing of that thing; or (iii) he intentionally aids, by acts or illegal omission, the doing of that thing.
These are essential to complete the abetment as a crime.
The word "instigate" literally means to provoke, incite, urge on or bring about by persuasion to do anything.
In cases of alleged abetment of suicide, there must be a proof of direct or indirect act/s of incitement to the commission of suicide.
It could hardly be disputed that the question of cause of a suicide,
particularly
in the context of an offence of abetment of suicide, remains a vexed one, involving multifaceted and complex attributes of human behavior and responses/reactions.
In the case of accusation for abetment of suicide, the Court would be looking for cogent and convincing proof of the act/s of incitement to the commission of suicide.

In the case of suicide, mere allegation of harassment of the deceased by another person would not suffice unless there be such action on the part of the accused which compels the person to commit suicide; and such an offending action ought to be proximate to the time of occurrence.
Whether a person has abetted in the commission of suicide by another or not, could only be gathered from the facts and circumstances of each case.
(By The Learned Public Prosecutor)

14.PW.3 Devaraj and PW.4 Bharath being the spot mahazar witnesses turned hostile and not supported the case of the prosecution regarding drawing of Ex.P2 mahazar in the place of occurrence.
Nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.3 and PW.4 to establish the contents of Ex.P2 mahazar.
15.PW.5 Kumar, being the family friend not deposed anything about the marriage took place between Bhuvaneshwari and accused, and he is totally ignorant about the facts of the case.
Except his visit to Victoria Hospital to see the dead body.
He is not aware as to why Smt.Bhuvaneshwari committed suicide.
He denies the statement given before the I.O., marked as per Ex.P.6.
16.PW.6 V. R. Manjunatha, Police Sub-Inspector, Jnanabharathi P.S., deposed regarding receipt of Ex.P1 complaint, forwarded the FIR to the jurisdictional Court as per Ex.P7 and PW.7
Narasimhaiah, Police Sub-Inspector, Jnanabharathi P.S., visited the place of occurrence, drawn Ex.P2 Mahazar, in the presence of mahazar witnesses.
Prepared inquest in the presence of inquest mahazar witnesses, as per Ex.P4.
Collected MO1 to MO5, and filed PF to the jurisdictional Court.

17.PW.8 Basappa, turned hostile and noit supported the case of the prosecution regarding alleged torture meted out by the deeased, when the deceased and accused were residing at Vijayanagar,
Bangalore.

He denies the statement given before the I.O., marked as per Ex.P8.
18.The
very complainant has not supported the case of the prosecution regarding alleged harassment meted out by the deceased, and offence of abetment committed by the accused.

The oral testimony of PW.2 has not been corroborated by the other witnesses such as PW.3 Devaraj,
documentary evidence available on record marked as Ex.P1 Inquest and Ex.P5 PM Report reveals that death is due to asphyxia as result of hanging, but physical and mental harassment soon before the death has not been proved by the prosecution beyond all reasonable doubt.
Accordingly I answered points No.1 and 2 in the Affirmative.
19. Point No.3:

In view of answer of court on points No.1 and 2, this court pass the following:

The Bail and Surety bonds of accused stand canceled.
